raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year like I always do...

I'm an old man now, 70 years. My back hurts in the morning and my eyes don't see so good. I've been putting seed in this dirt for 50 years — since I was a little boy following my own father. Twelve mu is all we have. Not much, but it feeds the family and puts a little cash in my pocket when the grain truck comes.

My wife helps me, and my son comes back from the city at harvest time. He works construction in Shijiazhuang now. My grandson is in school. So it's mostly me and the old woman in the field day-to-day.

**The wheat first** — I always plant wheat around Cold Dew (寒露), that's what my father did and what everybody in the village does. Some of the young ones now, they plant a week later because they say the weather's warmer now, but I stick with my timing. I buy seed from the same fellow in town — regular local variety, not those expensive new seeds. My neighbor Old Wang tried some fancy seed two years ago and it didn't do any better than mine, so why spend the extra money?

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of the compound (the 15-15-15 kind, 40 kg bag) per mu before I plow. That's what I can afford. Then when the wheat greens up after winter and starts to jointing, I scatter urea — maybe 15 kg per mu, by hand. If the wheat looks yellow or thin, I put a bit more. If it looks strong, a bit less. You can see it with your eyes. I don't need anybody to tell me.

Water from the well — I water before winter so the ground doesn't freeze dry, then again at green-up, and one more time around heading if the rain doesn't come. The electricity for the pump costs money, so I don't water more than I have to. Three times is usually enough.

Weeds — my son-in-law's brother sprays for me, I pay him a bit. One spray for weeds in spring. That's all. I don't mess with the bug sprays unless I see something bad.

Harvest is around Dragon Boat Festival time, early June. I hire the combine — everybody does now, can't do it by hand anymore, my back won't take it. 80 yuan per mu or so.

**Then maize, right away** — no time to rest. The maize has to go in the same week the wheat comes out or you lose heat units in autumn. I hire the little planter, they come through the village. I use regular hybrid maize seed from the shop, whatever they're selling that year. Cost me about 40 yuan per mu.

For the maize I don't do base fertilizer separately — no time, and the ground still has some goodness from the wheat. I put urea down once when it's knee-high, about 20 kg per mu. If there's a dry spell I pump water once or twice, but summer maize mostly lives on rain. Last few years the rains have been okay.

Harvest the maize late September, before the autumn rains make the kernels sprout. Hire the combine again.

I don't expect big yields. Maybe 400 kg of wheat per mu in a decent year, 450 kg of maize. Some years less if the spring is too dry or a bad wind flattens the wheat. You can't control weather, you just do what you always did and hope.

Money is tight. I don't borrow. If the fertilizer shop wants too much money in autumn, I buy less and hope for the best. Better to have some grain and some cash in the drawer than to gamble.
